questions.q: According to this lesson, how does a governance strategy differ from a governance architecture?
options: The architecture describes the target state and principles; the strategy describes the sequenced, funded plan to get there
They are the same document with two different names
The strategy replaces the need for an architecture entirely
The architecture is only used after the strategy is fully executed
questions.explain: The lesson draws a clear line: architecture is the design, strategy is the plan — sequencing, funding, and sponsorship.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four questions a real governance strategy document must answer?
options: How is it funded and sponsored?
What font should the strategy deck use?
Which vendor logo goes on the cover page?
How many meetings will be scheduled this quarter?
questions.explain: The four questions are: where are we now, where are we going and why, what's built first, and how is it funded and sponsored.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a strategy without a named executive sponsor is really just a proposal?
options: Because it has no mechanism to get funded or defended when priorities compete
Because proposals are illegal without sponsorship in most companies
Because only executives are allowed to read strategy documents
Because unsponsored strategies are automatically deleted by IT policy
questions.explain: Without a sponsor attached, there's no one accountable for funding or defending the plan when it competes with other priorities.

questions.q: What does the lesson identify as a common way governance strategies fail?
options: Trying to govern every domain and platform at once instead of sequencing priorities
Focusing on too few initiatives in the first year
Having too many named executive sponsors
Documenting the maturity assessment too thoroughly
questions.explain: Attempting centralized governance over everything simultaneously stalls — most organizations need to sequence and choose where to start.

questions.q: Per this lesson's roadmap for the chapter, what does Lesson 23 cover next?
options: Turning the strategy into a time-sequenced roadmap
How to run a technical SQL interview
Choosing a cloud storage vendor
Writing Python unit tests for a pipeline
questions.explain: Lesson 23, Governance and Architecture Roadmaps, is exactly that — sequencing the strategy's priorities over time.
